conviction_note: Two independent lines — external air-price data and Navan's own prior-year sequential seasonality — both say the $219-221m Q2 guide is mechanically low for a business that takes a rate on booking dollars, against a tape that is down 7% into the print with puts bid; sized well inside the 14.06% implied move because this is the third consecutive quarter of the same beat-and-raise setup and the market's reaction to it has already decayed from +43% to +8.4%.

findings.finding: US airline-fare CPI averaged +26.2% y/y across May-July 2026 (Navan's fiscal Q2) versus +14.2% y/y across Feb-April 2026 (fiscal Q1), and the seasonally-adjusted index rose 6.4% sequentially between those two windows (291.3 avg to 310.0 avg) — a ~12pp step-up in the dollar-price tailwind to gross booking volume inside the quarter management guided to 28% revenue growth, down 12pp from Q1's 40%.
findings.why_not_priced: Navan's revenue is a take rate on booking dollars, so ticket-price inflation flows through GBV and usage revenue almost mechanically, yet no preview maps a macro CPI series onto a Feb-Jan fiscal calendar — the Q1/Q2 split (Feb-Apr vs May-Jul) is not a calendar quarter and the step-up is invisible unless you cut the series that way. If it were priced you would not see the stock down 7.19% over 20 days and 25-delta skew at +5.64 vol points into a print where the guided revenue growth rate falls by exactly as much as the price tailwind rose; you would see call skew and a run-up.
findings.independence: Delta's CEO on 2026-07-10 said higher airfares would persist and reported corporate travel up in the June quarter with record corporate sales (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/10/delta-air-lines-dal-q2-2026-earnings.html); BofA separately modelled United Q3 unit revenue +15.6% on 'price hikes working their way through the booking curve' (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/bofa-sees-delta-united-entering-191300683.html). Amex GBT, the same demand pool, reported transactions +45% and TTV +57% on 2026-08-04 and reiterated FY guidance (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260804630662/en/American-Express-Global-Business-Travel-Reports-Strong-Q2-2026-Financial-Results). Partial offset from the same BLS release: lodging away from home fell 2.8% m/m in July and the lodging index dropped from 195.7 in May to 185.9 in July, so the hotel leg of GBV is roughly flat-to-down sequentially — I have netted that into the sizing.
findings.monthly_detail: Airfare CPI y/y: Feb 2026 +7.1, Mar +14.9, Apr +20.7 (Q1 avg 14.2); May +26.7, Jun +26.5, Jul +25.5 (Q2 avg 26.2). Table: https://www.usinflationcalculator.com/inflation/airfare-inflation/ . SA index levels from FRED CUSR0000SETG01: Feb 283.495, Mar 291.073, Apr 299.267, May 307.305, Jun 307.963, Jul 314.803.

findings.finding: Navan's Q2 FY27 guide of $219-221m implies exactly 0% sequential revenue growth off Q1's $220m, whereas the same fiscal quarter a year earlier grew +9.1% sequentially ($157.5m to $171.9m); repeating last year's own seasonality would put Q2 at roughly $240m, i.e. +40% y/y — the same growth rate Navan just printed — against a guide of +28%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 FY26 revenue base is not in any wire recap: Navan has never reported a standalone Q2 as a public company (it IPO'd 2025-10-30), so $171.9m only exists as a subtraction of the Q1 FY26 comparative in the Q1 FY27 release from the six-month figure buried in the S-1. Previews therefore anchor on the y/y guide rate rather than on the sequential shape, and management's stated rationale — a 'seasonally slightly weaker summer season' — is contradicted by the company's own prior-year seasonality, which was seasonally stronger. If the market had done this arithmetic the guide would be treated as a floor and the stock would not be trading below where the CEO's 10b5-1 plan sold nine sessions ago.
findings.independence: Arithmetically self-verifying against a second document: the S-1 gives six-month FY26 revenue of $329.413m (usage $299.698m + subscription $29.715m) at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1639723/000162828025042130/navan-sx1.htm ; $329.413m less the $157.5m Q1 FY26 comparative is $171.9m, and $220m / $171.9m is 28.0%, which reproduces the company's stated Q2 guide growth rate exactly. Note this finding shares the Q1 FY27 press release with nothing else here, but it points the same direction as the airfare finding above and should not be added to it at full weight — the two are separate evidence for one conclusion, that the guide is low.
findings.context: FY26 revenue $702.27m vs FY25 $536.84m (+30.8%); FY27 guide $907-913m raised from $866-874m at Q1, and FactSet consensus at the time was $871.7m (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/navn-navan-expects-fiscal-2027-revenue-range-907m-913m-vs-factset-est-of-871-7m-ce7f5cdbdc8bff23).

findings.finding: CEO Ariel Cohen sold 393,378 shares at $30.1441 on 2026-08-27 — 168,378 personally plus 75,000 from each of three GST trusts, all three of which went to zero holdings — nine trading sessions before the print, and Lightspeed entities distributed roughly 2.5m shares in June at $19-20 and continued trimming in July.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline sale is on every insider screener, but the detail that all three family GST trusts were taken to zero rather than trimmed is only visible in the XML footnotes, and it establishes that a standing distribution programme is still running into and through the print — relevant supply for a name whose float is still short-dated post-IPO. Weak, deliberately: it is a Rule 10b5-1 plan and therefore carries no information about the quarter, which is why I have sized it near zero rather than as a directional signal.
findings.independence: Secform4's transaction log corroborates the June-July Lightspeed and officer selling sequence at https://www.secform4.com/insider-trading/1639723.htm . Nothing independent supports reading it as informed selling.

Any 8-K since 2026-06-26, which was a routine Item 5.07 annual-meeting vote — no pre-announcement, no management change, no material event in the run-in
CFO transition as a live issue — Aurelien Nolf (ex-Lyft FP&A/IR) has been in seat since 2026-03-02 and this is his second full quarter; fully covered at the time
The IPO securities class action (Levi & Korsinsky / Hagens Berman, N.D. Cal., lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-04-24) — all of it is March 2026 news and the stock has tripled off its $8.51 low since
Navan status page and outage history for May-July 2026 — only routine provider degradations (May 5, May 8, May 15, Jun 3, Jun 8, Jun 10), nothing that would show up in a quarter

Trustpilot / PissedConsumer / Capterra review sentiment — chronic complaints about disruption support and duplicate charges, but the same complaints exist across 2024-2026, no inflection I could date to this quarter
Hiring-page headcount as a spend or growth tell — Navan's own openings page renders client-side and returns no count; third-party aggregators disagree wildly (59 vs 72 vs 244), so nothing usable
A secondary or resale registration landing on the print — only the 2025-10-30 S-8 reoffer prospectus for employee shares, nothing new

Company-specific cause for the ~11% drawdown from $30.14 on 2026-08-27 to $26.85 today — no news, no filing, no downgrade; sell-side targets were being raised through it (BofA $26 to $34 on 2026-09-02, Oppenheimer to $35, Citizens to $38)
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline on both counts: the 20-day run-up is -7.19% and the 25-delta skew is +5.64 vol points with downside paid, while the evidence I found points to a guide that is low on two separate arithmetics — though I discount for the fact that the baseline's directional read is itself thin here (3,367 contracts of total open interest and an ATM spread 43% of mid make 'downside paid' a weak statement), and for the stock already sitting 12% off its high after tripling from the low, which means a third straight beat-and-raise is partly expected.
